This card was filed by the `os-dev` this seat dispatched for objectui#9083. Its body is correctly bare in every other respect — ⛔ unassigned, ⛔ no `pm:queue`, ⛔ no `priority:*`, and it says so — but it applied **`domain:devx`** itself. ⛔ Routing is triage's, not a filing seat's, and this lane's convention is that a finding is filed with no `domain:*` at all.

⇒ ⭐ **Treat this card as UNROUTED.** The `domain:devx` on it is the filing seat's suggestion, not a lane assignment, and it should be confirmed or replaced on its merits like any bare card.

⛔ **I have deliberately not removed the label myself.** This seat's standing limit is that it never produces *or changes* a `domain:*` — stripping one is as much a routing act as applying one, and correcting an overstep by committing the same class of overstep is not a correction. So the label stands and this comment is the correction; triage may of course remove it.

⚠️ One thing worth keeping whatever the routing: the measurement is the useful part and it carries its own firing control in the same run — `trim of '   *' === ''` is `false`, the JSDoc-separator leg returns the same hit as the no-separator control, and the truly-blank leg returns `[]`. ⇒ the empty result is a barrier, ⛔ not a dead scanner. The second half (the `CONT_WINDOW` docblock crediting a paragraph break for a blindness that distance 8 alone causes) is corroborated independently on objectui#9083, where that same misattribution turned out to sit in the card's framing too.

⭐ Read together with **objectui#9081** and **objectui#9083** before anyone touches `scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs` — three open cards now name that one file, and objectui#9081 blocks measurement on the other two: the census **refuses every run on `main`**, re-confirmed at `b775500af677ec876b5f6dad443028e7f9ed6fbf` (exit 1, same failing control as at `3984bab5a`). 同文件串行, ⛔ not parallel work.

## Contract review — **ACCEPT**. PR #9632 lands option **A**, which is the only option this card was allowed to land.

### ⭐ The strongest reading in this PR is the one I can verify without running anything

The diff on `scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs` contains **zero non-comment added lines and zero non-comment deleted lines** — I enumerated the patch hunks and filtered out every line whose content begins `*`, `//` or `/*`; both buckets came back **empty**. ⇒ the guard's behaviour is byte-identical **by construction**, and the dev's tree-wide "1271 rows before and after" is a corroboration of something the diff shape already proves rather than the only thing holding it up.

That also settles Clause-②: **0 new exports** in the patch, **0 files under `packages/**`**. `Clause-②: no` **verified in-seat**, both legs.

| CI at this reading | 23 success / 3 skipped / **7 `in_progress`** / **0 red** |

### Zone 2 assumption 1 — I was right, and it was worse than I framed it

I said the docblock credits the paragraph guard for a blindness that distance alone causes. The misattribution had reached **three** places, not the one I described: `CONT_WINDOW`'s docblock, the syntax-5 coverage paragraph that writes the two scope rules as one mechanism, and a test comment calling the fixture's separator "a second paragraph". The pinned fixture contains **zero** lines that trim to empty ⇒ there is no paragraph break there for any guard to act on, which is the cleanest possible form of the finding.

### Ruling on `open_questions[0]` — **A for this card. B is not refused; it is routed to objectui#9083.**

The card's author reserved "should the guard reach delimiter-only lines" **in writing**, as a judgement with a cost. ⛔ A dev passing by does not get to make a judgement the card reserved, and nothing measured here overturns the reservation — so landing A was correct and I am not asking for B in this PR.

⭐ What changed is that the cost is no longer unpriced: **B removes ZERO rows on today's tree**, byte-identical census output, against a positive control in the same harness where `CONT_WINDOW` 2 → 5 **does** move it 1271 → 1289. A zero with a discriminating control is a reading.

I am **not** filing B as a standalone card, and the reason is the dev's own: the two scope rules interact — if objectui#9083 widens the window, an inert paragraph guard matters **more**, not less. Deciding them together costs one decision instead of two. ⇒ the measurement goes onto **objectui#9083** as input to the decision already sitting there. ⛔ Posting a measurement is not grading that card and takes no position on the width.

### Ruling on `open_questions[1]` — **A, and the rule is the authority, not my preference**

`AGENTS.md` #9, quoted from `origin/main` this fire:

> when you declare something verified, **point at the instrument that re-derives it — the script, the gate, the test — and never write down its answer** … A figure that is still correct is the dangerous case, not the safe one

Replacing the rotted count with the command that re-derives it is that rule applied literally. ⛔ Option B (a fresh number with a date stamp) is the thing the rule forbids, and the figure's own history is the rule's worked example: it was a correct reading once and rotted silently, in **both** size and composition.

### ⚠️ Scope deviation, recorded rather than absorbed

The stale `CONT_WINDOW` count was repaired **in place** in this PR rather than filed. I accept it under the bounded-repair conditions — same defect class as the card (prose asserting something no instrument re-derives), same file, same gate family, no new verification surface, file unheld. ⛔ But it is a deviation from a dispatch word that named the guard and its docblock, so it is named here.

⭐ It also has a consequence the dev was right to raise loudly: **that figure is an input to objectui#9083's pending decision**, and this PR changes how #9083 will obtain it — from reading a number to running a command. That is strictly better under #9, but #9083's holder must not be surprised by it, which is the second reason for the cross-reference below.
